transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I’m here because lately, when I walk across campus, everything feels strange—like I’m looking at it through glass. I don’t feel fully in my own body, and the buildings and students around me seem slightly unreal. It scares me.
Do these feelings come on in sudden episodes?
It’s not really a sudden episode. It happens when I’m walking across campus, and then I start feeling like I’m behind glass—not quite in my body—and everything around me looks unreal.
When this happens, do you know that the strange, unreal feeling is just a feeling and that the campus is actually real?
Yes, I know the campus is real. It just doesn’t feel real in those moments—like I’m watching it through glass, and I’m not fully in my own body. That’s what scares me.
Did this start soon after something very frightening or traumatic happened to you?
Yes. It started after the lighting rig collapsed during the showcase. That was six days ago, and it’s been happening since then.
Have these unreal feelings made it hard for you to do your usual schoolwork or daily activities?
Yes. I haven’t been able to do my job normally. I walked out of a planning meeting, missed two mentoring sessions with students, and I’ve been avoiding parts of campus I’m supposed to use.
Since the accident, have you had unwanted memories of the lighting rig collapse that keep coming back?

Yes. The sound of the rig crashing down just comes into my head when I’m grading or making coffee. Then I see the volunteer on the floor and the students pushing forward, like it’s happening right in front of me again.
Since the accident, have you been avoiding reminders of the lighting rig collapse?
Yes. I’ve been taking the long way around campus so I don’t have to pass the atrium. And if someone brings up the showcase, I usually change the subject or leave before I have to talk about it.
Since the accident, have you been feeling unusually jumpy or easily startled?
Yes. If a door bangs or a cart rattles in the hallway, I jump so hard my chest hurts. Then I’m shaking for several minutes before I can get back to what I was doing.
